newsitem.title: THAILAND: FOCUS-Thai baht vulnerable despite rally - analysts.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Thai baht vulnerable despite rally - analysts.

text.p: A battle between Thai baht speculators and the central bank could erupt again despite the bank's recent stiff capital control measures, analysts said on Monday.

The baht has rallied in the offshore market as foreigners, hit hard by Bank of Thailand measures to cut off baht supplies to them from local sources after the mid-May speculative attack on the currency, sold dollars heavily to buy the Thai unit.
Since the controls were imposed, a two-tier baht market has been in place.
The Thai currency rallied to 24.800/24.850 to the dollar at midday in the offshore market compared with the central bank's midrate of 25.81.
In the domestic market, the baht steadied at around 25.820/25.840 in quiet activity, dealers said.
"I don't think speculators have given up. They are just patient and waiting for an opportunity (if the measures are lifted)," said one dealer at a U.S. bank.

But the central bank has given no indication of any let-up. In a May 28 circular it told commercial banks, finance and securities firms to stop foreign exchange transactions with foreign institutional clients that could contribute to speculation in the baht.

The central bank said financial institutions should suspend all foreign exchange swap deals that give foreign partners access to baht funds, including currency and interest rate swaps, forward rate agreements, and currency and interest rates options.

"Offshore players heavily sold the dollar in the spot market to cover their baht short positions. They don't want to borrow in the swap market where interest rates for short-term baht are surging," said one dealer at a European bank.
The one-month baht/dollar swap premium was traded at 135/160 satangs per dollar at midday in offshore market compared with 120/140 in early morning.
Before the central bank's measures led to an informal two-tier foreign exchange market, the one-month swap premium was at around 6.00/10.00 satangs.

Currency dealers said in the first few days after the central bank introduced the measures, speculators betting with short forward baht positions faced prohibitive financing costs of over 1,000 percent a year to cover their baht/dollar contracts.

Analysts said the central bank was unlikely to lift its tough measures in the near term as weak economic fundamentals, a stock market at near eight-year-lows and lingering worries about problems in the finance sector had made the baht fragile.
"Removing the two-tier market with the economic outlook so bearish will merely open the doors for another run on the Thai baht," Singapore-based I.D.E.A. said in a new report.

Analysts said the central bank's measures, if they remained in plpace for a long period, would certainly affect foreign inflows into Thailand which needs external funds to finance its high current account deficit.

"Foreigners want hedging facilities and stability in foreign exchange rates if they want to invest in Thailand," said one dealer at a local bank. "Right now there is no liquidity in the forward market. The (dollar/baht) spot rate is also very different between offshore and domestic markets."
